findings.claim: The review's F3 blocked on a contradiction between TC-01-INT-09 and REQ-01-026 quoting text that no longer exists. The cases file changed after this run's plan was compiled; the case now agrees with REQ-01-026 and is implementable, so the finding was withdrawn rather than settled or halted on.

witness.detail: Hashing the bundle against the shas the handoff recorded: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md UNCHANGED; specs/portal/01-home.cases.md CHANGED, bf9ec62e925706174a57fa4266ef8b1a2f68b95dca1a4a1731f5d25ba9f42de8 → a03bcc84669732febdd561e3c38f3927453ec38003bdb7281c59166e9d95acd9; specs/portal/01-home.md unchanged at 40eca1daf21f6500a23ef3cd2ffba63df41fcc440547eb2b8286518476102261. The review quoted TC-01-INT-09 as expecting 'two member-anniversary entries with detail.years 1 and 2' and a member-joined for the backdated member. The current text reads: 'No member-joined entry whose subject is the backdated member — its joining is 731 days ago, outside REQ-01-026's window — and exactly one member-anniversary entry for it, with detail.years 2; its first anniversary falls 366 days ago and is outside the window too.' The test was rewritten to that.

findings.suggestedFix: Nothing in the documents needs to change. Recorded because a gate blocked on a revision that had already been repaired, and because a run whose plan pins bundle shas can be handed findings written against a different revision — the shas are the cheap check that says so.

findings.claim: Closing the review's CR-07 finding required five new PORTAL_MESSAGES keys for failure text, and the contracts' Error Messages table enumerates ten rows, none of them a failure sentence. The table no longer lists every message the area exports.

witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md §Error Messages lists ten rows — noProject, limitInvalid, cursorInvalid, groupsInvalid, settingsForbidden, feedEmptyTitle, feedEmptyBody, monthEmpty, requestsEmpty, noCountry — and every one is a success-path or refusal string. The review's blocking finding required that six inline sentences such as the Q1 failure banner's move into packages/validation, on the convention every other area follows (SIGNING_PROVIDER settings.saveFailed, HOLIDAY toastServerError, ENVELOPE_MESSAGES.generic). packages/validation/src/portal.ts now exports monthLoadFailed, feedLoadFailed, entryLoadFailed, settingsLoadFailed and settingsSaveFailed, which the table does not carry.

findings.suggestedFix: Either add the five failure rows to §Error Messages, or state that the table enumerates the messages the spec decides and that transport-failure text follows the shared convention without being listed. The second is probably right — no other area's spec lists its generic failure string — but it should be said once rather than inferred.

findings.claim: The screen replaces the holidays list with PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry whenever no country is stated, while REQ-01-019 answers that same caller the global holidays. On an organization holding a global holiday the screen says no calendar reaches the caller while discarding rows the body carried. Unchanged since attempt 5 and still true.

witness.detail: specs/portal/01-home.contracts.md:286 — 'Q1 answered, no country | The holidays list is replaced by PORTAL_MESSAGES.noCountry and a link to the profile.' specs/portal/01-home.md:175 — 'IF the caller's membership states no country, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer only the holidays whose countryCode is null.' Concrete case: an organization with one holiday whose countryCode is null, and a member whose membership states no country. GET .../portal/home answers holidays.countryCode null and holidays.upcoming carrying that row — TC-01-INT-07 asserts it. The screen draws the sentence in place of the list and never draws the row.

findings.suggestedFix: Either draw the sentence only when holidays.upcoming is empty, or stop answering global rows to a member with no country. The implementation follows the states table because that table is determinate; no case distinguishes the readings, because every case with no country also has no global holiday.

findings.claim: A foreign Postgres took port 5433 mid-session — the port every suite here is configured for — and produced E2E failures that read as product defects: 30-second navigation timeouts while the dev server logged 200s for the same URL. It also took the integration suite down between two runs of it.

witness.detail: `netstat -ano | grep ":5433" | grep LISTENING` returns two different PIDs (7152 and 5528). A direct pg connect from the host: `postgresql://devscribed:devscribed@127.0.0.1:5433/devscribed_dev` fails authentication, while `postgresql://devscribed:devscribed@127.0.0.1:5434/devscribed_dev` connects and answers `current_user = devscribed` — 5434 being the second port the project's own docker-compose publishes for the same container. `docker exec psql` succeeds against the container regardless, because it uses the container socket, which is why the container looked healthy. Before the workaround: integration `Error: P1000: Authentication failed` and e2e `client-participants` 3 failed. After pointing the untracked apps/api/.env at 5434: integration 19/19, and the targeted e2e 24 passed with no failures and no flakes.

findings.suggestedFix: Nothing in the product. Recorded because the failure was indistinguishable from a product defect for several runs, and because the lever already exists: both apps/api/test/database-url.ts and e2e/environment.ts honour TEST_DATABASE_URL and E2E_DATABASE_URL, and both fall back to apps/api/.env. A person who wants 5433 back needs to find what took it; nothing here killed it.

shardDecision: Thirteen review findings split by file set into three groups dispatched together — A (apps/api/src/portal plus its own suite), B (packages/validation and the five web screens, which interlock and could not be split further), C (the two e2e files) — with the lead holding the test runs and the commit. A fourth, A2, was dispatched mid-flight to correct A's brief on F3 after the lead checked the finding's witness against the bundle shas and found the cases file had moved: the contradiction the review blocked on had already been repaired in the document, so the answer was a rewrite rather than a halt. Two children then held apps/api/test/portal.spec.ts, which was a dispatch error; all three edits were verified intact afterwards.

shards.status: ok — superseded A's brief on F3
